Q083-01.notes: Group cost 12*11=132. Need 15n>132, so n>8.8 and the least integer is n=9 (135>132; n=8 gives 120<132). Traps: answering 8.8 or 8.

Q083-02.notes: T/n - T/(n+2)=30 gives T=15n(n+2). T/(n-1) - T/n=30 gives T=30n(n-1). So n+2=2(n-1), n=4, T=360. Check: shares 90, 60 (6 people), 120 (3 people).

Q083-03.notes: |(2C+30)-(1.8C+32)|=|0.2C-2|<=2, so 0<=C<=20. B is the one-sided distractor, D has the sign error, A uses the wrong tolerance. All distractors are well motivated.

Q083-04.notes: Slope=(3a-2a)/(2a-a)=1, so f(x)=x+a and f(5a)=6a. D assumes f is proportional (2x), C uses the ratio 1.5, A uses slope 1 with no intercept.

flags: Answer cue: A, B and C each contain an obvious overclaim ('not selected at random', 'exactly', 'most of the 600 seniors'), so D can be found by elimination. D is also the only hedged choice.
minor: closely resembles the official SAT sampling-variability items (several random samples with different means, choose the appropriate conclusion).
Q083-05.notes: Sampling variability; the average of the sample means is 6.96, so the true mean is likely near 7. C confuses the spread of sample means with the spread of individual values.

Q083-06.notes: 52% of 7000 is 3640. R has 0.46*5000=2300 and needs 1340 more out of 2000, which is 67%.

Q083-07.notes: Total 180. The 4 smallest sum to 40 and the 4 largest to 108, so the 5th and 6th values sum to 32. Median=(5th+6th)/2=16.

flags: minor: C is an implausible distractor (unequal group sizes are clearly not a flaw), which leaves effectively three choices.
Q083-08.notes: Comparing only the people who completed the program with the full control group breaks the random assignment, since those 55 selected themselves. B is about generalizing to all employees, not about causation. D (placebo) is the strongest distractor.

Q083-09.notes: 1200*60/2500=28.8. A=1200/2500 (per second), B is the inverted ratio, D=28.8*60 (per hour). A flow of 1,200 m^3/s is plausible for a large river.

Q083-10.notes: In the same time t, A rides 18 km and B rides 12 km. After meeting, A covers 12 km in 1.2 h, so vA=10 km/h and t=1.8 h. Then vB=12/1.8=20/3 km/h, and B needs 18/(20/3)=2.7 h. Check with t^2=t1*t2: 3.24=1.2*2.7.

flags: minor: the stem says 'about', but the answer 3.4 is exact; 'about' is unnecessary.
minor: distractor A (2.5) has no clear error path, so it is easy to eliminate. C (ignores the 85% health) and D (uses 60% as the charge) are well motivated.
